messages:
nina-customer: Hey team — saw intermittent JSON parse errors in production when customers use JSON mode with streaming. Happens ~1-2% of requests. Example parse error from our frontend: "Unexpected token { in JSON at position 143".

sara-support: Sorry you're hitting this, nina. Can you paste a redacted sample of the raw stream you received (the exact bytes) and the request headers you used? Also does this happen with non-streaming?

nina-customer: Pasting a truncated raw stream we captured (newlines kept):
```
data: {"id":1,"result":{"name":"Alicia"}}
data: {"id":1,"result":{"name":"Alicia","age":30}}
data: {"id":2,"result":{"name":"Ben"}}
# but sometimes we get this merged blob:
data: {"id":1,"result":{"name":"Alicia"}{"id":2,"result":{"name":"Ben"}}
```
The client JSON.parse fails when we try to parse per-event. Non-streaming mode seems OK (no merge seen). Headers: `Authorization: Bearer ***`, `X-Redwood-Client: webapp`, `X-Redwood-Enable-JSONMode: true`, `Accept: text/event-stream`.

sara-support: Thanks. Mike on runtime is looping you in. We'll take this to eng. Meanwhile, can you share a session id and whether you use any custom caching/proxy between client and API?

mike-eng-runtime: Looking at the merged example — that looks like two SSE events concatenated without a boundary. Could be a flushing/batching race where a streaming flush happens while a prefix/KV cache write is interleaving bytes. Did you enable prefix caching or request-level batching on your account?

nina-customer: We use default batching. No external proxy. Session id: session_9d3f. We do have client-side retry that replays smaller chunks but that shouldn't affect server-side streaming.

mike-eng-runtime: Can you repro with this curl (from your network):
```bash
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \n  -H "X-Redwood-Client: webapp" \n  -d '{"model":"rwd-xyz","input":"make two separate json objects","json_mode":true,"max_tokens":40}' \n  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```
Watch for any events that show broken boundaries. If you can repro, attach the exact raw bytes.

zane-ml: Hypothesis: when JSON mode + streaming + batching are combined, the streaming flush path may not always serialize buffer boundaries if two responses share the same batch window. If the KV/prefix cache update and stream flush interleave, you can see cut-and-append results like the merged blob.

mike-eng-runtime: For triage: (1) set `batch_size=1` or disable automatic request batching from your client; (2) try toggling `X-Redwood-Prefix-Cache: off` header as a short workaround; (3) if you must keep batching, switch to non-streaming JSON mode until we patch.

sara-support: Nina, can you try the curl above and also re-run with `-H "X-Redwood-Prefix-Cache: off"` and report back with the raw capture? If it clears up we have a high-confidence workaround.

nina-customer: Will try now, sending results shortly. Thanks.

ops-bot: Ticket created: INC-2026-7834 — assigned to eng-runtime. Priority: P2. Link: https://redwood.internal/tickets/INC-2026-7834

mike-eng-runtime: Internal note for the team: look at streaming writer logic (stream_flush()) and prefix cache commit path (kv_shard_commit()). Suspect missing mutex or atomic flush ordering when two responses share a batch. Also check SSE framing (we expect `data: ` newline separation).

zane-ml: Adding that we should add a regression test that fuzzes chunk boundaries under concurrent batch flush and KV commit. Also add a guard to ensure a single stream flush completes before any cache blob append.

sara-support: Nina — any update from your repro attempts?

nina-customer: Repro successful with curl when batching left on — got merged blob twice within 15 minutes on staging. With `X-Redwood-Prefix-Cache: off` the stream boundaries look clean. Confirmed workaround.

sara-support: Great — we'll keep you posted. Engineers will push a gated fix and we'll notify you when the patch is deployed. We'll also check billing impact and whether any malformed streams caused downstream parsing retries.

mike-eng-runtime: I'll follow up in the incident ticket with a patch plan: (A) add lock around stream flush + cache commit, (B) add unit/regression tests, (C) deploy canary with streaming-heavy traffic.

ops-bot: INC-2026-7834 updated: status -> investigating.

sara-support: Thanks everyone. Nina — we'll continue the thread in the ticket but feel free to ping here if you see anything else. :thumbsup:
